slides.headline: One letter just destroyed this family.
slides.sub: Augustus Egg, Past and Present No. 1, 1858

slides.headline: London, 1858
slides.text: A comfortable London drawing room, 1858. It looks like an ordinary afternoon. But something has just happened here. Look for the clues.

slides.headline: The letter
slides.text: The husband sits frozen, a letter in his hand. It has just told him everything: his wife has been unfaithful.

slides.headline: On the floor
slides.text: His wife lies collapsed on the carpet at his feet, her face buried in her arms. She cannot even look at him.

slides.headline: Gold chains
slides.text: Look at her wrists: gold serpent bracelets, almost like handcuffs. And in the dark, under his shoe, lies a crushed portrait of her lover.

slides.headline: The apple
slides.text: On the table, an apple cut in two. One half is pierced by a knife, the other has rolled to the floor near her.

slides.headline: House of cards
slides.text: Meanwhile, their two little daughters play, unaware. Their house of cards, built on a French novel by Balzac, is collapsing.

slides.headline: The open door
slides.text: And in the mirror, the door stands open, as if she is already leaving. Egg painted two more scenes of what came next.

slides.headline: Condemn or pity?
slides.text: Years later he is dead, and she is homeless by the Thames, holding a baby. Egg never judged her. Would you?
